meta.purpose: Single source of truth for game content. The engine implements the small vocabularies below (traits, effects, statuses) once; new content should reuse them. If an entry needs a new verb, add it to the vocabulary first.

status_meanings.phase2: Needs the camp or the server (Phase 2). Keep it in the file, don't spawn it yet.
status_meanings.later: Designed and held for a later content batch.
status_meanings.concept: Idea only. Needs design before use.

meta.never_delete: Mark retired content "status": "retired" instead of deleting it, so old floors and runs still load and replay.
meta.text_rules: "text" is hand-written flavor, 120 characters max. Rules text ("HP 4 · Hits 1d3 · Fast") is generated from the stats at display time, never hand-written, so it can't go stale.

rules.movement: 8-directional, for the player and monsters alike, with no corner cutting: a diagonal step is blocked when either tile it passes beside is a wall; a diagonal attack (or disarm) out of a 1-wide doorway needs only one of them open. Tap a tile to walk there by the shortest path; stop early whenever something new comes into view. D-pad remains as an option.
rules.turns: Player acts, then monsters, using ROT.Scheduler.Speed. Speeds: slow = 50 (acts every other turn), normal = 100, fast = 200 (acts twice per player turn).
rules.damage: roll(attacker's weapon or natural dice) - roll(0 to defender.armor), the armor rolled fresh on every hit, minimum 1 on a hit.
rules.natural_regen: None. Walking and waiting heal nothing. HP comes back from health potions, bandages, food and a worn item's regen. Monsters don't regenerate.
rules.hp_between_floors: HP and ailments carry down the stairs, with no rest heal (decided 2026-10-13). After a death the next floor starts at full HP with no ailments. Phase 2: the camp is where you heal.
rules.holding_ground: When one side steps into the other's reach (beside it, any of the 8 neighbors), the one already there gets the edge: if its next action is an attack on the newcomer, the hit roll is made twice and the better one counts. Only hunting monsters get it. An equal-speed chaser still can't hit someone who keeps moving away.
rules.field_of_view: ROT.FOV.PreciseShadowcasting with the creature's sight radius. The player sees a tile in that line of sight only while it's lit (rules.lighting). Tiles once seen stay drawn but dimmed (explored). Monsters notice the player by line of sight alone; light doesn't hide anyone yet.

lighting.always_lit: The start room and the guardian's room, each with a torch over the player's or guardian's column.

monster_states.asleep: Doesn't move. Each turn the player is within 2 tiles, 50% chance to wake. Always wakes when hit or alarmed.
monster_states.wander: Random walk. Starts hunting when it has line of sight to the player within its sight radius.
monster_states.hunting: Chases by A* path. After 8 turns without seeing the player, goes back to wandering.
monster_states.hidden: Ambusher. Doesn't move or show until the player comes within its sight radius, then hunts.

traps.detection: At the start of each player turn, every hidden trap within 1 tile is revealed with chance = search% + the trap's detect_mod. The lantern reveals adjacent traps automatically.
traps.disarm: Beside a known, armed trap, disarming takes a turn and works with chance = search% + 30 + the trap's detect_mod. A success earns 2 XP. The omen doesn't change it. A failure sets the trap off on you, as if you'd stepped on it.
traps.monsters: Monsters never trigger traps. They live here.
traps.ghost_reveal: Traps your partner triggered or detected on this floor are revealed for you (Milestone 4).

floor_budget.monsters: 7 + floor(floor number / 2), max 13. A group counts as its members.
floor_budget.special_rooms: 0 to 2, rolled from the rooms list.
floor_budget.exit: One exit ladder, placed in the farthest third of the floor by path distance from the start.

loot.per_player: Layout, monsters and traps come from the shared floor seed. Item rolls (chest contents, drops) use the floor seed plus the player's slot (A or B), so the two of you find different things in the same places. This is what makes trading worth doing.
loot.deck: A chest's item is drawn when it's opened, from a deck the character carries, one per rarity: an item doesn't come up again until every other item of its rarity has. The kit's starting gear starts drawn. A monster's rarity drop draws from the same deck. A death starts a new deck.
loot.pity: After 4 chests in a row that gave commons, the next one gives uncommon or better.
loot.stash: Content 16. Cover with 'hides' (straw) hides a stash in a patch with its chance: one tile of the patch, shared by both players, holding a gold pile's worth rolled per player. Stepping onto it finds it and picks it up in the same move. When the cover burns out, the gold is left in the open.

death.phase1: The floor ends and the run is recorded.
death.phase2: You wake at camp with half HP and lose the gold you found that day.
death.retry: In practice and checks, a death offers Continue?: the same floor again from its start. You come back in your gear, with the level, XP and HP you came down with, but at least 1/3 of your max HP (rounded up). Your grave sack lies where you fell: it holds the items and gold the floor gave you, and keeps 95% of the XP you earned there (rounded down). Die again before you reach it and it's gone. Monsters come back; one you killed gives no XP or drops again. The daily floor keeps one attempt.

art.motion_format: art.motion names how a kit or monster moves a tile (one of art.motions); without one it slides plainly. Lengths are map pixels (a tile is 8), times are ms. ms: the travel. ease: linear, in, out or in_out. hop: arc height, hops: arcs per tile. steps: travel in that many jerks (0 = smooth). tilt: degrees it rocks. stretch: how much it stretches along the way. land_ms and land_squash: a squash on landing, after the travel. ms + land_ms stays under 200 (tap-walk's step).

stomp.text: Heavy and sure: lifts a little, lands hard.

flutter.text: Bobs up and down the whole way.

scamper.text: Hunched and shifty, rocking side to side.

ooze.text: Stretches toward where it's going, then catches up.

lurch.text: A wooden bound, then a thump.

trudge.text: Too heavy to hurry, swaying as it comes.

style_rules: 8x8, opaque, ink background. Ink inside the sprite works as outline and negative space.
At most 5 non-ink colors per sprite.
Creatures face the viewer, roughly symmetric, filling about 6x6 to 8x8.
Weapons and wands point diagonally from bottom-left to top-right.
Potions and vials are upright and centered, cork or neck on top.
Readable at 1x: within one biome, no two enemies share both silhouette and main color.
Never rely on color alone to tell two things apart. Shape must differ too (accessibility).
art.generator_prompt_template: {size}x{size} pixel art roguelike {kind} sprite: {silhouette}. Key features: {features}. Colors: {colors}. {pose}. Opaque background {ink_hex}. Hard pixels, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no dithering. Use only this palette: {palette_hex_list}.
art.set_piece_prompt_template: {width}x{height} pixel art scene: {scene}. Mood: {mood}. Same palette as the game ({palette_hex_list}), ink background, hard pixels, no anti-aliasing. Characters drawn as in their 8x8 sprites but larger: {characters}.

set_pieces_planned.scene: two travelers at a campfire in a cave mouth, packs set down, embers rising
the Rat King on a heap of barrels, crown askew
one frame per story beat, defined with the story skeleton

erratic.does: Each move, with this chance, steps to a random open adjacent tile instead of toward its target.

steal_gold.does: On a hit, takes this much gold instead of dealing damage, then flees toward the exit and leaves the floor if it gets there. Drops everything it stole when killed.

on_hit_status.does: When its attack hits, applies the status with this chance.

ranged_status.does: If the player is in line of sight within range and the cooldown is ready, spends its turn applying the status at range instead of moving.

disguised.does: Drawn exactly as the prop and doesn't act until the player bumps, opens or attacks it. Then it reveals itself and gets a free attack.

reassemble.does: On death leaves a bone_pile that rises again with full HP after the delay, up to 'times', unless the killing blow came from a weapon with unless_tag.

split_on_hit.does: When hit and it survives with at least min_hp left, splits into two copies, each with half its remaining HP (rounded down) and half its XP.

death_cloud.does: On death, fills tiles within radius with a cloud for 'turns' turns. Anything standing in it gets the status.

heals_allies.does: When off cooldown, heals the most-hurt ally in range instead of attacking.

flees_when_adjacent.does: Steps away when the player is adjacent, if it can.

hunts_by_sound.does: Ignores sight. Moves toward the most recent noise within hearing range (combat, traps, breaking things). A player who waits in place makes no noise.

summons.does: Every 'every' turns, spawns one 'enemy' adjacent to itself, up to max_alive at once.

shared_hp.does: Guardian. One HP pool shared by both players across days. Damage either of you deals is saved when your run ends; the guardian floor repeats daily until the pool hits 0. Until Phase 2, each player fights a normal copy.

reach.does: Weapon. Can attack an enemy up to 'range' tiles away in a straight line with nothing in between.

ranged.does: Weapon or wand. Attacks a visible enemy within range. Adjacent attacks use the melee numbers instead.

stun_on_hit.does: Weapon. Hits apply 'stunned' with this chance.

charges.does: Limited uses. One comes back every 'every' turns until it's full; the recharge rule says the rest.

params.turns: n (optional: the status's default_turns, which may be "rest of floor")

params.ignites: true to light the flammable cover in the area (optional)

params.dmg: dice, or a whole number for a flat amount

statuses.label: Rooted
statuses.text: Stuck fast. You can still swing.

statuses.label: Burning
statuses.text: On fire. It's as bad as it sounds.

statuses.label: Fed
statuses.text: Something in your stomach. The ache eases, slowly.

statuses.label: Hidden
statuses.text: They can't see you. Don't push it.

statuses.label: Soaked
statuses.text: Wet to the knees. Slower to dodge, and very hard to set alight.

statuses.label: Blessed
statuses.text: Something old is on your side tonight.

kits.name: Warden
kits.role: Front line. Takes hits and holds corridors.
kits.text: Sword, leather, two health potions. Stands in the corridor so nothing gets past.

kits.name: Lamplighter
kits.role: Scout. Sees further, spots traps, fights at range.
kits.text: Bow, cloak, lantern. Sees it coming, and sees what's underfoot.

biomes.name: The Cellars
biomes.text: Old cellars under the ruin: barrels, bones and rats.

guardian.layout: One great hall with two side rooms.
guardian.exit_rules: Phase 1: the ladder down is there from the start; the guardian is optional, for its loot. Phase 2: a ladder back up is always available (retreat to camp, damage is banked), and the ladder down appears only when the shared HP pool hits 0.

biomes.name: The Fungal Hollows
biomes.text: Caves where the fungus has gotten ideas.

guardian.layout: A round cavern ringed with spore pods.

biomes.name: The Drowned Halls
biomes.text: Flooded halls of whoever built all this. The water is not empty.

generator.extra: Add shallow water pools from the sheet's water tiles (columns 11-13, rows 6-8). Water ends burning.

biomes.design_notes: Ideas: eels that only attack from water tiles, drowned sailors, crabs (sheet tile [12, 0]), an imp (tile [11, 1]) or the eye creature (tile [13, 0]) as the guardian.

cellar_rat: Death by rat. Not a big rat. Just a rat.
The rats send their regards. Also their cousins.
Outnumbered by things the size of a shoe.
The rats were hungry. The rats are no longer hungry.
Last seen kicking at rats. The rats kicked back.
Nibbled to death. It took a while.
Thought the rats were the easy part.
The cellar's rats have a new story for their pups.
Death by a thousand nibbles. More like forty.
cave_bat: Killed by a bat that wasn't even flying that way.
The bat zigged. They zagged. Badly.
Swung at the dark. The dark had wings.
Couldn't pin down a bat. Few can.
The bat never flew in a straight line. Neither did the swings.
A bat, then another bat, then this stone.
Their aim was true. The bat's path wasn't.
Swatted at a bat for the last time.
skeleton: The skeleton got back up. They didn't.
Should have crushed the bones. Now there are more bones.
Fought a skeleton. Became one, eventually.
The skeleton didn't stay down. Neither did the damage.
Turns out the dead hold grudges.
Outlasted by something with no organs.
Killed by someone who'd already done this part.
The skeleton had practice at this.
goblin_cutpurse: Robbed, then killed. The goblin insists on the order.
{gold} gold left behind, and a goblin who knows it.
The goblin took the gold, then the rest.
Chased a thief into a corner. The corner had friends.
Died fighting for their purse. The purse is fine.
The goblin says thanks for the gold. And everything.
Lost their gold, then their footing, then the rest.
A goblin with sticky fingers and sharp knives.
Paid the goblin tax. In full.
The goblin ran. They followed. Bad idea.
The cutpurse cut more than purses.
web_spinner: Held perfectly still for the spider. Very considerate.
Saved the spider a lot of walking.
Caught in a web, then caught up in it.
The spider had patience. They didn't.
Wrapped up and put away for later.
Walked into the web. Stayed for dinner.
Eight legs, one plan, no escape.
cellar_ooze: Cut the ooze once, then twice, then it was just math.
Cut the ooze in half. Now there were two problems.
The ooze multiplied. Their HP didn't.
Every swing made more ooze. They kept swinging.
Died in a puddle with opinions.
Fought the ooze, then the ooze's children.
Too much ooze, not enough sword.
Now part of the floor, in a sticky way.
chest_mimic: Opened the chest. The chest opened back.
Died doing what they loved: looting.
Reached for the loot. The loot reached back.
Greed is a chest with a tongue.
Treasure? Teeth. The teeth were the treasure.
Trusted a chest. Never trust a chest.
The chest was hungry, and they were in it.
Eaten by the thing they came to rob.
A box full of teeth and bad news.
rat_king: Would not kneel to the Rat King. Got knelt on.
Killed by royalty. Technically an honor.
The Rat King's court found them guilty.
The crown belongs to the rats. So does this body.
Long live the king. Not them.
Royal guard: rats. Royal verdict: dead.
Tried to take the crown. Got the crowd.
The king's subjects are well fed tonight.
Treason against the rats, punished by the rats.
spike_plate: The floor had teeth. Now it has a story.
Watch your step, they said. They didn't.
A loose flagstone, a short story.
The plate was set. So were they.
Found the trap. With their feet.
The flagstone had been waiting for years.
snare: Held fast while the company arrived.
flame_jet: You smell it first, they say. They had a cold.
Hot air, and then very hot air.
The wall breathed fire. They breathed smoke.
A whoosh, a glow, a tomb.
Should have noticed the scorch marks.
The jet fired once. Once was plenty.
shrine: The shrine asked for blood. They gave it all of it.
Prayed for strength. Paid in full.
The gods take tithes in HP.
Asked for a blessing. Got an invoice.
Knelt at the shrine. Didn't get up.
The shrine took everything. It always does.
fire_flask: Threw the fire flask. Then walked into it.
A fine throw. Everyone near the landing agreed.
Their aim was perfect. Their position wasn't.
Hot potato, hot hands, hot everything.
Lit the room. Starred in it.
The flask did its job beautifully.
Too close to their own masterpiece.
poisoned: Every breath stung, and then there weren't any more.
Death by something green. Mostly by breathing.
Something green, then nothing at all.
Poison works slowly. It still works.
Breathed the wrong air one breath too long.
The sting was small. The rest wasn't.
Venom, patience and a bad finish.
burning: Went out in a blaze. Not figuratively.
Ashes to ashes, faster than usual.
Stop, drop and roll. Skipped all three.
The floor smells like a cookout now.
Found the water a turn too late.
fire: Stood in the fire to see what would happen. This happened.
Lit the straw. Admired it from much too close.
The straw went up. So did they.
Admired the blaze from the inside.
Played with fire. Lost to fire.
Too warm, then much too warm.
Burned the straw, the room and the hero.

context.line: Died with {count} health potions. Saving them for a special occasion.
{steps} steps from the ladder. So close it's rude.
Couldn't take {gold} gold with them. They tried.
Turn {turn}. A personal best, in the wrong direction.
Saw every corner of floor {floor}. The last one was occupied.
Very good armor. Lovely tomb.
Invisible for exactly one swing too many.
Level {level}. Killed by a rat. We don't talk about it.
Floor one. Everyone starts somewhere. They also stopped there.
Rang the doorbell. Everyone answered.
The rune sent them somewhere. Somewhere was busy.
Packed the antidote. Admired it, mostly.
Carried everything. Used none of it.
Saved {count} potions for later. Later never came.
{count} health potions, unopened. Collector's edition.
Thirsty, with {count} potions in the pack.
The ladder was {steps} steps away. It waited.
Could see the ladder from here.
{steps} steps short of finishing floor {floor}.
Died rich. {gold} gold, nowhere to spend it.
{gold} gold in the pack. You can't take it with you.
The richest body on floor {floor}.
Turn {turn}. Barely got their boots dirty.
A short visit. Turn {turn}.
Lasted {turn} turns. A brisk death.
Mapped the whole floor. Missed one thing.
Explored everything, including the afterlife.
Iron plate. Iron coffin.
Dressed for battle. Battle didn't care.
Hidden from everyone but the thing that killed them.
Unseen, unheard, unbreathing.
Level {level}. Undone by vermin.
A level {level} hero. A level one rat.
Didn't make it past the welcome mat.
Floor one, and the tutorial was rough.
The first floor's first casualty. Today.
Stepped on the glyph. The whole floor came running.
Woke the neighbors. The neighbors had teeth.
Teleported into a bad decision.
Vanished from danger, reappeared in worse.
Poisoned, with an antidote in the pack. Classic.
The cure was in their pocket the whole time.
Saved everything for a rainy day. It rained.
A full pack and an empty life bar.
Try {attempt}. Same floor, same ending.
Try number {attempt}. The floor is getting to know them.
Back for more. Got more.
Died here before. Liked it so much they did it again.
Practice makes perfect. Not yet, though.
The floor remembers them. Fondly, and with teeth.
Try {attempt}. Persistence is a virtue. So is caution.
Deja vu, with extra death.
Came back stronger. Not strong enough.
The rematch went like the match.
Their sack was right there. Right. There.
So close to the sack they could smell the gold.
Died reaching for their own stuff.
Within arm's reach of their sack. Not quite arm's reach.
The sack waited. It's still waiting.
One more step to the sack. One step.

generic: Death by {killer}, who says it was self-defense.
Last words: "I can take one {killer}."
Went down swinging. Mostly missing, but swinging.
Brave, bold, and one step too close to a {killer}.
The {killer} doesn't even know their name.
Nobody saw it coming. Least of all them.
Fought bravely. Lost anyway. That's the dungeon.
Here by choice. Stayed by accident.
Took the stairs down. Kept going.
They had a plan. The plan had a hole.
Brave enough to go first. Unlucky enough to stay.
Optimistic to the last turn.
It seemed like a good idea at the time.
Should have waited a turn.
One more step, they said.
Tried their best. The dungeon tried harder.
Here lies a hero, give or take the hero part.
Did not read the room. The room read them.
Never ran. Should have.
Ran. Not fast enough.
The floor was hungry. They were nearby.
Died as they lived: underground.
They came, they saw, they were seen.
Gone, and the torches didn't even flicker.
Their last turn was their worst turn.
A promising career, briefly.
Not the hero this dungeon needed.
Felt lucky. Wasn't.
Turn {turn}: a bad one.
Floor {floor} sends its condolences. Not really.
Level {level}, and still learning.
Rest now. The dungeon won't.
In the end, the dark won the argument.
Gave it everything. Everything wasn't enough.
Died doing what they loved: guessing.
Bravery: high. Health: zero.
Their story ends here. A short book.
Out of HP, out of luck, out of turns.
Their pack outlived them.
Cause of death: the dungeon. Contributing factor: also the dungeon.
Saw the danger. Waved hello.
They had one job. It was surviving.
Somewhere, a bard is softening this story.
Fearless. That was the problem.
The dark took notes.
Went looking for trouble. Found it on the first try.
Not the first to fall here. Won't be the last.
Their footsteps stop here.
A tactical retreat, into the afterlife.
Stood their ground. The ground won.
They're fine. They're just very, very still.
Tough as nails. Nails bend.
The death was quick. The walk here was the long part.
Here rests a person with excellent intentions.
Leveled up in spirit.
Just resting their eyes. Permanently.
Some heroes fall. This one also tripped.
They'd like to speak to the dungeon's manager.
The torchlight remembers them fondly.
Down, but the story isn't over. Probably.
Their courage outlasted their HP.
Kept a level head. Lost everything else.
If found, please return to the surface.
May the next one learn from this one.
Remembered by the rats. Fondly.
Score: the {killer} 1, hero 0.
Lost an argument with a {killer}.
Underestimated the {killer}. Once.
Met a {killer}. It went badly for one of them.
Their last view: the {killer}, up close.
Thoughts and prayers from the {killer}. Mostly prayers.
Turned their back on the {killer}. Briefly.
Proof that the {killer} is not to be trifled with.
Tried diplomacy with the {killer}. It declined.
Was winning against the {killer}, right up until the end.
Bested by a {killer}. History is written by the {killer}.
Final opponent: the {killer}. Final mistake: also the {killer}.
"A fine meal," says the {killer}.
The {killer} will tell this story for years.

lead: Your sack's right where you dropped: {loot}.
The floor is holding {loot} for you.
In a sack by your last footprint: {loot}.
Somebody has to pick up {loot}. It's you.
In a sack with your name on it: {loot}.
The floor kept {loot} warm for you.
The sack remembers {loot}. So should you.
A sack on the floor holds {loot}.
close: Mind the thing that did this.
Don't die on the way. Seriously.
It's not going anywhere. You might be.
The floor keeps nothing for long.
The dungeon's lost and found closes soon.
Try not to add to the pile.
Die again first and it's the rats'.

no_sack: Nothing in your pockets. Lucky you.
Nothing to lose, which is something.
Empty pockets. Easy walk.
The floor gave you nothing. You gave it nothing back.
No sack this time. Travel light.
Nothing to pick up. Just pick yourself up.
You left with what you came with. Mostly your dignity.
Clean slate, empty hands.
Nothing to fetch. That's efficiency.
You found nothing, and nothing is exactly what you lost.
Not a coin to your name down there.
Broke, but not broken.
The floor kept nothing of yours. It's a little insulted.
No sack. No stakes. No excuses.
Pockets empty, slate clean.
Nothing to recover but your pride.
Zero loot, zero loss. Perfectly balanced.
You owe the floor nothing. It disagrees.
Nothing in the sack, because there's no sack.
All you lost was time.
Light pockets, heavy lesson.
No sack to chase. Just the floor.
Your pockets were honest: empty.
Nothing dropped but your guard.
You traveled light. Too light, maybe.
No loot lost. A rare clean death.
Nothing to go back for except the ladder.
The floor got nothing out of you. Rude.
Nothing ventured, nothing lost. Something died, though.
An empty-handed death. Very minimalist.
lost_sack: Your old sack? Gone. The rats split it.
The last sack didn't wait for you.
Your old sack is somebody's bed now.
The first sack? Finders keepers. They found it.
That sack is gone for good. So it goes.
Two deaths, one sack. The sack lost.
Your old sack has been redistributed.
The floor took back what it gave. All of it.
Your sack wandered off. Sacks do that.
The rats held a meeting about your sack. It went well for them.
Your old sack is now a rat's retirement fund.
The last sack belongs to the dungeon now.
Somewhere down there, a goblin is very pleased.
Your previous sack sends its regards from a rat nest.
That sack's gone. Nobody saw anything.
Lost the sack too. Momentum.
The old sack? Never heard of it, says the floor.
Your last sack has been eaten. Including the sack.
Gone: one sack, contents and all.
The dungeon kept the change.
The sack got tired of waiting.
Your sack has left the building.
That sack is a story now. A sad one.
The rats split it evenly. They're fair like that.
Old sack: lost. Dignity: also lost.
No refunds on the old sack.
The last sack is gone. Respect the new one.
The bats took the sack. Nobody knows how.
Your old sack has entered the food chain.
Sack lost. The floor sends no apology.

lead: Back in a blink, with {hp} HP.
Back on your feet at {hp} HP.

shaken: Shaken, and it shows in your aim.
Shaken up and sent back down.
A bit shaken. Who wouldn't be?
Shaken all the way to your elbows.
sore: Sore in places you didn't know you had.
Sore, and the floor knows it.
Sore, like after a long day of dying.
Sore. Every dodge is a negotiation.
grim: Grim: you hit harder, duck less.
Grim. Bring the anger, mind the dodge.
Grim and ready for a rematch.

omen_rules: One omen per floor, rolled from the shared floor seed so both players get the same one. Guardian floors never roll an omen. Show the omen's text when the floor starts and in the message log. Effect keys: sight_mod_all (added to everyone's sight, minimum 2), light_mod_all (added to every light's radius, the player's included, minimum 1), extra_monsters, extra_traps, extra_items (added to the floor budget), xp_mult, gold_mult, ember_mult (multipliers), monsters_start (overrides every monster's start state), detect_mod (added to trap detection), ghost_full_path (show the partner's whole route from the start).
